higher: A high level can happen when you are short of fluids, live at a high altitude, smoke, or have some lung or blood conditions.
lower: A low level is often called anaemia. It can come from low iron, blood loss or a long-term illness, and can make you feel tired, pale or short of breath.

higher: White blood cells rise when the body is fighting an infection or has inflammation. Stress and some medicines can raise them too.
lower: A low count can follow a viral illness or come from some medicines or conditions. It can make infections more likely.

higher: Platelets can rise after an infection, inflammation or an iron shortage, and sometimes for other reasons.
lower: A low count can make you bruise or bleed more easily. Viral infections, some medicines and other conditions can cause it.

higher: Sugar above the usual range can be linked to diabetes or pre-diabetes. One reading can also be raised by a recent meal, illness or stress.
lower: Low sugar can cause shaking, sweating and confusion. It can happen with diabetes medicines, long gaps between meals or other causes.

higher: Sugar after a meal above the usual range can be linked to diabetes or pre-diabetes. What and how much you ate also matters.
lower: Low sugar can cause shaking, sweating and confusion. It can happen with diabetes medicines or long gaps between meals.

lower: Low sugar can cause shaking, sweating and confusion. It can happen with diabetes medicines, long gaps between meals or other causes.

higher: This test shows your average sugar over about 3 months. A higher value means sugar has been running high, and is linked to diabetes or pre-diabetes.
lower: A low value is unusual. Some blood conditions or recent blood loss can affect this test.

higher: Creatinine is cleared by the kidneys. A higher level can mean the kidneys are working less well, or that you are short of fluids. Muscle size and some medicines also change it.
lower: A low level is usually not a concern and can be seen when muscle mass is low.

higher: A higher number is usually fine.
lower: eGFR estimates how well your kidneys filter your blood. A lower number means they are filtering less. Doctors watch it over time, together with other tests.

higher: Urea can rise when you are short of fluids, eat a lot of protein, or when the kidneys are not clearing waste well.
lower: A low level can be seen with a low-protein diet, liver problems or pregnancy.

higher: This can rise when you are short of fluids, eat a lot of protein, or when the kidneys are not clearing waste well.
lower: A low level can be seen with a low-protein diet, liver problems or pregnancy.

higher: Too much potassium can affect the rhythm of the heart, so doctors take a high value seriously. Kidney problems and some medicines can raise it.
lower: Low potassium can cause weakness and cramps and can affect the heart. Vomiting, diarrhoea and some water tablets can lower it.

higher: A high level usually means the body is short of water.
lower: A low level can come from too much water, some medicines, or illnesses of the kidneys, heart or liver. It can cause tiredness and confusion.

higher: Bilirubin is a yellow substance the liver clears. A high level can turn the skin or eyes yellow and can be linked to liver or bile problems, or to the breakdown of red blood cells.
lower: A low level is not usually a concern.

higher: ALT is a liver enzyme. A higher level can mean the liver is irritated, for example by fatty liver, an infection or some medicines.
lower: A low level is usually not a concern.

higher: AST is an enzyme found in the liver and also in muscle. A higher level can mean the liver or muscles are irritated, for example by fatty liver, an infection, some medicines or hard exercise.
lower: A low level is usually not a concern.

higher: A higher level means more fat in the blood, which over time can raise the chance of heart and blood-vessel problems. Food, weight, activity and family history all play a part.
lower: A low level is usually not a concern.

higher: LDL is the cholesterol that can build up in blood vessels. A higher level can raise the chance of heart and blood-vessel problems over time.
lower: A low level is usually not a concern.

higher: A higher level is generally considered helpful.
lower: HDL helps clear fat from the blood. A low level can raise the chance of heart and blood-vessel problems over time.

higher: Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood. A higher level can be linked to eating a lot of sugar, fat or alcohol, extra weight, diabetes or family history.
lower: A low level is usually not a concern.

higher: A high TSH often means the thyroid gland is underactive (making too little hormone), which can cause tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold.
lower: A low TSH can mean the thyroid is overactive (making too much hormone), which can cause a fast heartbeat, weight loss and feeling hot.

higher: A higher reading is usually fine.
lower: This shows how much oxygen your blood is carrying. A lower reading can mean your lungs or heart are not getting enough oxygen into the blood.

higher: A high reading means your heart is pushing harder against your blood vessels. Over time this can strain the heart, kidneys and brain. One reading is not enough to say you have high blood pressure.
lower: A low reading can cause dizziness or fainting in some people and is fine in others.
